title: NSDR for Early Recovery Signal
description: A light-touch NSDR nudge when sleep duration and HRV both dip modestly below your personal baseline — an early autonomic recovery signal, well short of a full recovery deficit. No training change is recommended at this tier.

conditional.question: Did last night's sleep and readiness look a bit off?
conditional.yesLabel: Yes, add a short NSDR to today

actions.timing: Early afternoon or whenever a break is available
actions.details: A brief guided NSDR session to support parasympathetic recovery. Optional — this tier is a light nudge, not a strong signal that training or plans need to change.

benefits: Supports early-stage autonomic recovery before it compounds
Low time cost, no disruption to planned training
Builds the habit of responding to small deviations before they become large ones
science: Mild simultaneous dips in sleep duration and HRV relative to one's own baseline are commonly used as early, low-confidence indicators of accumulating physiological strain. NSDR (Non-Sleep Deep Rest) protocols promote parasympathetic activation and are Huberman Lab's standard low-cost recommendation for supporting recovery without requiring behavior change elsewhere.
contraindications: Not a substitute for addressing a real sleep debt
Do not use as justification to skip planned training at this tier alone — signal is weak

learning_resources.title: Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR) — Huberman Lab official page

evidence_metadata.scientific_rationale: Two-signal (sleep duration + HRV), both below 90% of personal rolling baseline for one night. Two independently-measured signals moving the same direction is a weaker but still meaningful early indicator of reduced recovery capacity, consistent with general autonomic-nervous-system-strain literature (lower HRV and reduced sleep duration both associate with elevated sympathetic tone).

evidence_for_protocol.notes: Huberman Lab directly and repeatedly recommends NSDR/Yoga Nidra as a general-purpose tool for supporting recovery and offsetting the effects of a poor night's sleep. This part of the recommendation (NSDR is a reasonable, low-risk response to reduced recovery) is well supported by the source material.

evidence_for_trigger.notes: The specific choice of 90%/90% baseline-percentage thresholds, the two-metric combination, and the 1-night persistence window are NOT independently validated — they are a product heuristic chosen to catch early signal with low specificity while keeping the recommendation itself low-stakes (an optional relaxation nudge, not a training change). Should be tuned against real user outcome data once n-of-1 tracking exists.

expected_effect.short_term: Modest reduction in subjective stress/fatigue same day; unlikely to be measurable on the ring itself within 24h.
expected_effect.long_term: If used consistently at this tier, may reduce the frequency/severity of escalation to the high or severe recovery-deficit tiers below, though this is untested.
